info.title: Kash Engine API
info.description:
Read-only access to the Kash Engine data: daily reports, scored news, IPOs, the market
prediction, companies and the delivery log.

## Authentication

Send a token in the `Authorization` header:

    Authorization: Bearer ke_<prefix>_<secret>

Make a token on the **Account** page of the web app. The secret is shown once. A signed-in
browser session also works (this is how the Swagger page calls the API).

## Access rules

The API follows the same rules as the web app. A user needs the feature of an endpoint, and
needs an active subscription if the site requires one.

## Errors

Errors use `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457). Branch on the `code` member.

## Limits

Each token has a request limit for each minute. The headers `RateLimit-Limit`,
`RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` show the state. A client over the limit gets `429`
and `Retry-After`.

## Versions

The version is in the path. Inside `v1` changes only add things. The `API-Version` header gives
the full version of the contract.

get.description:
Return `ok` and the version of the API contract. It needs no sign-in.

Use it for a simple uptime check. It does not test the database.

get.summary: Get the caller, the subscription and the features
get.description:
Return who is calling, the subscription state and the features that the caller may use.

Every signed-in user may call this endpoint, also a user whose subscription ended. It is the
best first call to check that a token works.

get.description:
List the daily reports, newest first.

There is one report for each date. The list has no report text. Read one report to get it.

**Required feature:** `reports`.

Return the report of one date, with its full text and its data.

The `day` is a date like `2026-10-07`. The answer is `404` if no report exists for it.

**Required feature:** `reports`.

get.description:
List IPOs with their dates, price band, GMP, subscription and score.

The score and the verdict come from the scoring step. An IPO without enough data has the
verdict `unknown`. This is an analysis aid and not investment advice.

**Required feature:** `ipos`.

Return one IPO with the inputs of its score.

`signals` lists each input that the score used. `notes` says why an input was left out.
The answer is `404` if the IPO does not exist.

**Required feature:** `ipos`.

Return the newest prediction for the target index (Nifty 50).

`confidence` shows how strong the signal is. It is not a probability. Compare it with the
numbers of `/markets/accuracy`. The answer is `404` before the first prediction exists.

**Required feature:** `markets`.

get.description:
List predictions, newest target date first, with the real result when it is known.

**Required feature:** `markets`.

get.summary: Get the accuracy of the predictions
get.description:
Return how often the predictions were right, and the baseline to compare with.

The baseline always guesses the most common real direction. A useful model must beat it.
Trust the numbers only when `enough_results` is true.

**Required feature:** `markets`.

Return the newest saved close of each enabled instrument.

An instrument with no saved quote is left out. The list is short, so it has no paging.

**Required feature:** `markets`.

List the attempts to send a report, newest first.

The recipient is masked. The error text is only for staff users, because it can name an
internal setting. Other users see the status only.

**Required feature:** `delivery`.
